newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific sees more Minnesota rail woes.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific sees more Minnesota rail woes.

text.p: Union Pacific Corp said it was expecting more rail service problems near the Minneapolis-St Paul, Minn. area and southward this week due to rising waters on the upper Mississippi and Minnesota rivers.

"Our main line between the Twin Cities and Mankato (Minn.) is presently open, however, we expect that in the next day or so our tracks to go underwater if the rivers continue to rise as predicted," Union Pacific spokesman Ed Trandahl said.
"We expect our main line from the Minneapolis-St Paul area to Chicago to remain open," he added.

The St Paul Army Corp of Engineers office said the Minnesota River was forecast to crest April 14 at 716 feet above sea level at Savage, a Minneapolis suburb, which would be 18 feet above flood stage. As of late Sunday, the river was 708.5 feet above sea level.
Some grain elevators in the Savage area will halt operations this week as a result of rising river water and flooded rail lines, grain company officials said.
"We are shut down in the sense that we cannot serve a lot of our customers who are located on those river systems," Trandahl said of the flooding impact on Union Pacific's operations there.
